newsitem.title: USA: Proxy firm urges Nomura auditors' rejection.
newsitem.headline: Proxy firm urges Nomura auditors' rejection.

text.p: A U.S. investor service has urged Nomura Securities Co Ltd shareholders to reject the scandal-plagued company's slate of internal auditors.

Institutional Shareholder Services said the four nominees' ties to Nomura were too strong to let them monitor the new board effectively. Shareholders will vote on the slate at Friday's annual meeting.

"We strongly recommend that shareholders withhold support for all four nominees, and press the company to appoint truly independent auditors who can forestall future scandals by objectively monitoring the activities of Nomura's new board," Japan analyst Bruce Babcock wrote in a June 16 report.
Nomura, Japan's biggest securities firm, has been rocked by a scandal involving alleged payoffs to a corporate racketeer by company executives. The scandal has already led to a dozen arrests.
Babcock wrote that appointment of internal auditors and audit committees are required by law to provide independent monitoring of the board and improve accountability.
"However ... this new role is not yet functioning. Like many other Japanese companies, Nomura's appointments meet the letter of the law but not its spirit," he said.
Babcock said the four auditor nominees -- two independent and two non-independent -- had longstanding ties to Nomura, limiting their effectiveness.

For example, one of the independent nominees had been appointed an internal auditor at Nomura in 1982 before being reclassified as an independent. He is a director and president of one Nomura subsidiary and is chairman of the board of another.
The two nonindependent nominees "have worked for Nomura Securities all of their lives ... as well as serving on the board of that company," Babcock wrote.

Institutional Shareholder Services is an proxy advisory firm based in Bethesda, Md., and is a unit of Thomson Financial Services Group. It has 400 clients, mainly institutional investors and money managers.
